result:
Summary: The DRAGIN framework dynamically decides when and what to retrieve during the text generation process of Large Language Models (LLMs). It identifies the optimal moment to activate the retrieval module (deciding when to retrieve) and crafts the appropriate query once retrieval is triggered (determining what to retrieve). The framework consists of two components, RIND and QFS, designed to make decisions based on the LLM’s real-time information needs. It aims to overcome the limitations of traditional RAG methods, which often rely on static rules and limit retrieval to the LLM’s most recent sentence or tokens.
